'''Kakutani's theorem''' is a result in [[geometry]] named after [[Shizuo Kakutani]].  It states that every [[convex body]] in 3-[[dimension]]al space has a circumscribed [[cube]], i.e. a cube all of whose faces touch the body.{{r|k}} The result was further generalized by [[Hidehiko Yamabe|Yamabe]] and Yujobô to higher dimensions,{{r|yy}} and by Floyd to other circumscribed [[parallelepiped]]s.{{r|f}}

==Kakutani's theorem on 2-spheres== 

Given a continuous function <math>f:S^2\to\mathbb{R}</math>, there exist orthonormal basis <math>u,v,w</math> of <math>\mathbb{R}^3</math> such that <math>f(u)=f(v)=f(w)</math>.

The proof relies crucially on the fact that the fundamental group of <math>SO(3)</math> is finite: <math>\mathbb{Z}_2</math>, while the fundamental group of <math>S^1</math> is infinite cyclic: <math>\mathbb{Z}</math>.

This result easily implies the theorem on inscribing convex bodies in cubes.
